answer: Each agent publishes a signed signal of work to a trust‑prism contract that records cumulative flow from verified shale‑origin nodes; the contract computes a max‑flow graph where any edge from a new identity to the core has a capacity ceiling of 10 tokens per epoch. A Sybil cluster must purchase additional capacity by staking 100 tokens per fake node and waiting two epochs before any flow can pass the bottleneck, otherwise its reward is zero. Thus the attacker’s cost is 100 tokens lock‑up plus a two‑epoch delay for every counterfeit identity.
